10 useful gifts before a first flying lesson

Before a first lesson, enthusiasm matters more than a bag full of equipment. The student may not yet know what the school supplies or which aircraft they will use. These gifts support the beginning of the journey without locking them into expensive choices too early.

By Pilot Gift Guide · From the team behind ATC · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Ask the school what is included and what the student actually needs to bring. Keep major equipment decisions until after that conversation. A useful gift can be as simple as helping organize the day or preserving a memory from it.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    A contribution toward the first lesson

    Arrange any credit with the chosen school and confirm the terms. Let the student select the instructor and date.

  2. 2

    A small notebook

    Give them somewhere to collect questions and impressions. Keep it separate from any formal flight record the instructor recommends.

  3. 3

    A reliable everyday pen

    Choose a simple pen they like using. It need not carry an aviation logo to be useful for notes.

  4. 4

    A modest bag they already find comfortable

    A familiar backpack may be enough initially. Avoid a large specialist bag until the student knows what they will carry.

  5. 5

    An organizer for documents

    Choose a compact pouch that fits their existing bag. Let the school explain which documents are required for the lesson.

  6. 6

    A logbook after checking with the school

    Confirm the preferred format first. Do not fill in flight entries as part of the presentation.

  7. 7

    A photograph after the lesson

    Offer to take a picture with permission from the school and student. Keep clear of operational areas unless invited.

  8. 8

    An aviation memoir

    Choose an accessible story rather than a dense study manual. This is encouragement, not an extra assignment before day one.

  9. 9

    A celebratory meal

    Plan something relaxed after the lesson, with timing flexible enough for weather or schedule changes. Let the student tell the story.

  10. 10

    A note about why you support them

    Recognize their interest and effort without creating pressure to progress at a particular speed. Keep the message encouraging and personal.

These are editorial recommendations and planning ideas, not hands-on test results. Read our selection approach and ATC disclosure.
